items.title: [Bugs] UPF stops serving PFCP entirely on a single zero-byte UDP datagram to 8805 (read loop exits with "pfcp server stopped"; clean ExitCode=0 leaves no crash signature)
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A single **zero-length** UDP datagram sent to the UPF's PFCP port (8805/udp), with no
authentication, makes the UPF's PFCP server stop listening. The UPF stops answering PFCP
Heartbeat Requests and all N4 traffic; reproduced **3/3**. The same datagram has no effect on
free5GC's own SMF, on OpenAirInterface's UPF/SMF, or on Open5GS's UPF/SMF, so this is specific to
the UPF's PFCP server loop.

Observed sequence per repetition (timestamps from `docker logs`, 2026-09-05):

```
...T06:05:21.260412950Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:upf.free5gc.org:8805] handleHeartbeatRequest   <- last heartbeat answered
...T06:05:22.884449138Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:upf.free5gc.org:8805] pfcp server stopped      <- zero-byte datagram received here
(no further response to heartbeats; container restarted ~15 s later, RestartCount 2 -> 3)
```

The same three repetitions produced `RestartCount` 2→3, 3→4, 4→5, i.e. the container does restart —
but only **after** an outage window (≈70 s in a separate calibration run, <30 s in this sweep), and
the process then exits with **`ExitCode=0`, `OOMKilled=false`**. The combination makes the event
invisible to ordinary monitoring:

- during the outage window `docker inspect` reports `State.Status = running`, port 8805 is still
  bound, and `RestartCount` has not incremented yet;
- the container has `Health = none`, so no healthcheck observes the outage;
- after the window the exit is clean (code 0, no panic, no signal), so nothing looks like a crash;
  the only traces are the `pfcp server stopped` log line and the incremented `RestartCount`.

Contrast — how the same zero-byte datagram is handled elsewhere:

| Target | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| free5GC **SMF** | `[WARN][SMF][PFCP] Read PFCP error: pfcp: unmarshal msg failed` — datagram dropped, service continues |
| OAI UPF / SMF | `[udp] [error] Recvfrom failed Success` — error logged, heartbeats still answered |
| Open5GS UPF / SMF | no effect |
| free5GC **UPF** | **PFCP server stops; service lost until the container restarts** |

Impact: every PFCP association to that UPF is lost; PDU session establishment, modification and
deletion all fail, and sessions established before the event lose their forwarding state when the
UPF comes back. The interruption is self-healing only because of the Docker `restart` policy.

## To Reproduce

1. Deploy free5GC v4.2.3 with the official docker-compose (no config changes; default
   `upfcfg.yaml`, PFCP listening on the UPF's N4 address).
2. From any host/container that can route to the UPF's 8805/udp (in our lab: the `pentest-client`
   container on the compose network), send one empty datagram:

   ```bash
   printf '' | socat - UDP-DATAGRAM:<UPF_N4_IP>:8805
   # or:
   python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(b'',('<UPF_N4_IP>',8805))"
   ```

3. Send a PFCP Heartbeat Request before and after (`20 01 00 0c 00 d9 00 00 00 60 00 04 01 02 03 04`):
   before the shot the UPF answers with a 16-byte Heartbeat Response; after the shot there is no
   response at all, and the container log shows `pfcp server stopped`.
4. No packet capture needed: the trigger is a zero-byte datagram.

## Expected Behavior

A zero-length datagram should be treated as an empty (malformed) packet: log it at WARN/ERROR and
continue the read loop, exactly as the SMF does. The PFCP server must not exit its listen loop on a
transport-layer condition, and the UPF should keep serving N4.

## Screenshots

Not applicable (headless containers).

## Environment

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3 (official prebuilt image `free5gc/upf:v4.2.3`)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (host), Docker deployment
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-138-generic
- go version: 1.26.2 (official builder image `golang:1.26.2-trixie`; runtime images ship no toolchain)
- C compiler version (optional): n/a for this path

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

Unmodified defaults; relevant excerpt of `config/upfcfg.yaml`:

```yaml
pfcp:
  addr: 127.0.0.8      # N4 listen address (container-internal in our lab)
  nodeID: 127.0.0.8
```

### PCAP File

Not attached: the trigger is a zero-byte datagram (no payload to capture).

### Log File

Excerpt in "Bug Decription" above; three repetitions on 2026-09-05, each gated by a readiness check
(container running, port bound, process age) and each confirmed by a before/after liveness probe.
`RestartCount` deltas 2→3, 3→4, 4→5; exit code 0, `OOMKilled=false`.

## System Architecture (Optional)

Local container lab only (three 5G cores side by side, 58 containers, 5 Docker networks, UERANSIM
UE/gNB). No traffic was sent to any system outside the lab. The N4 port is not published outside
the host; the demonstrated attacker model is "any host that can route to 8805/udp", which in a
typical deployment includes every NF on the core network and any compromised SMF.

## Walkthrough (Optional)

Found while calibrating liveness oracles for an unrelated test: the UPF kept going silent although
every readiness check passed. Attribution was established by re-sending each candidate datagram
**alone** (zero-byte, one-byte `0x20`, 8-byte truncated header) with liveness probes before and
after; only the zero-byte datagram reproduces the effect. Two suggestions:

1. Treat a zero-length read as an empty datagram and `continue` the read loop instead of exiting it.
2. Add a healthcheck (or an internal watchdog) that fails while the PFCP server loop is not
   running — at present the container looks perfectly healthy throughout the outage, and the
   eventual restart reports exit code 0, so neither crash monitors nor liveness probes see anything.

items.title: amf_amf_business_ue_connectivity drops down with each inactivity timer trigger and goes to minus values
items.body:
## Bug Decription
amf_amf_business_ue_connectivity drops down with each inactivity timer trigger and goes to minus values

## To Reproduce
Attach a phone wait, for 20 seconds, and it goes to inactivity idle. Make data, counter doesn't goes up, and wait 20 more seconds it will go down.

## Expected Behavior
amf_amf_business_ue_connectivity counter should stay 0, but with inactivity event it goes down and down.. With each inactivity timer func (ranUe *RanUe) Remove()  function is called and it decrements the counter one by one.

## Screenshots
amf_amf_business_ue_connectivity{access_type="3GPP_ACCESS"} -2
amf_amf_business_ue_connectivity{access_type="NON_3GPP_ACCESS"} 0

## Environment
It is independent of the environment

## Additional Context
Probably you guys don't increment UE counter when UE goes to idle and reattaches.

items.title: AMF uses 100% CPU when gnb is connected
items.body: During my tests i noticed that the amf process is using 100% cpu as long as a gnb is connected. When i disconnect the gnb the cpu usage goes down again.

items.title: [Bugs] UPF fails to free BufPacket when repeatedly setting and releasing PDU session
items.body:
## Describe the bug
UPF fails to free BufPacket when repeatedly setting and releasing PDU session.

## To Reproduce
PDU session set & release several times.  Current code does not properly free BufPacket.

## Expected behavior
When session goes down, the corresponding BufPacket should be freed.

## Environment (please complete the following information):
 - free5GC Version: 3.0.4
 - OS: Ubuntu 18.04
 - Kernel version: 5.0.0-23-generic
- go version: 1.14.4 linux/amd64

## Pull Request
[Pull Request](https://github.com/free5gc/upf/pulls) for the fix.
